question_text: In the Command Pattern, how is reversible execution (Undo/Redo) architected to prevent memory bloat over deep history stacks?

options.text: Store complete system memory snapshots on disk at every command
Store delta/memento operations with an execution log and enforce a bounded circular buffer (e.g., max 50 states)
Re-execute all commands from initialization on every undo
Disable garbage collection during undo sequences

answer_explanation: Commands encapsulate inverse delta transitions rather than full system copies, and bounded circular deques bound memory consumption by pruning oldest historical states.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: Commands encapsulate inverse delta transitions rather than full system copies, and bounded circular deques bound memory consumption by pruning oldest historical states.
